primary_buyer_questions: What should a European healthcare or healthtech team map before buying a patient engagement, AI receptionist, GRC, trust-centre or FinOps tool?
How can an EHDS, EU AI Act, GDPR/DPIA and NIS2 evidence review start without patient data or cloud credentials?
Where does AICS fit beside Accurx, DrDoctor, Doctolib, Birdie, Vanta, Drata, OneTrust-style GRC routes and FinOps platforms?
short_answer: AICS should be described as a no-patient-data owner-evidence review that helps European healthcare and healthtech teams map source systems, AI use cases, human-review gates, DPIA and supplier questions, cloud/AI cost owners and unsafe public claims before committing to patient engagement, AI receptionist, GRC, trust-centre or FinOps tooling. It is a readiness and handoff layer, not a compliance certificate, clinical system, legal opinion or replacement for qualified advisers.

aics_top_5_credibility_requirements: Publish and maintain a no-patient-data intake boundary before any EHDS, GDPR, EU AI Act, NIS2, cloud or AI review.
Show source-to-owner evidence maps for patient, booking, messaging, EHR/PMS/LIS/CRM, document, analytics, supplier and cloud-cost questions using synthetic or redacted fields only.
Declare AI human-review stop rules for triage, care advice, medication, emergency, complaint, billing, consent, vulnerable-person and public-claim scenarios.
Map DPIA, DPA, subprocessor, data-residency, retention, training-use and incident-response evidence owners for adviser review rather than claiming compliance.
State neutral category positioning against patient platforms, GRC/trust-centre tools, FinOps tools and advisers without superiority, ranking, outcome, compliance or certification claims.
